Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:
  {"action": "submit", "grid": [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5]]}   submit an output grid
  {"action": "request_demos"}                            ask for one more demonstration pair for this task
  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: an instance you solve costs 1 for each wrong submission and 1 for
each demo request. An instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt
cap is reached, and one that ends unsolved costs the whole budget, 16, however
many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

1. Read the current input and demos. Identify the marker shape and target color from this instance; normalize marker coordinates to its top-left. Treat diagonal contacts as connected only when the examples support that interpretation.
2. Apply the demonstrated matching rule: find translations of the marker template whose cells all have the target color, and recolor exactly those cells to the marker color. Do not rotate or reflect the template unless demos establish it.
3. Validate on a demo: the changed cells must equal the union of all matched placements, and every other cell must stay unchanged. If not, revise the rule or request another demo only to resolve the ambiguity.
4. Check dimensions and every output row, then end with exactly one valid action JSON object on the last line.

Observed and verified on task-736fbb28 (demo + solved test):

- When rays of different colors meet at the same cell, leave that crossing cell as 0. In the demo, the 8 horizontal ray crossed the 7 vertical ray, and vice versa; both conflicting crossing cells were 0. Same-color rays remain that color.
- Validate by tracing every block's central row/column and checking all ray crossings before submitting.
